I'm Vance, team lead on MusterGo (NYP × SCCCI AI Challenge) — a React/Vite + Node/Express + Postgres delegation-attendance app. I own Screen 4 (AI Document Parsing / Onboarding + QR Boarding Passes) and Screen 6 (Trip Assistant, now evolved into "MusterChat"). Continue my work.

## Repo & ownership
- Working dir: C:\Users\cropt\Documents\Projects\VJMDynamics-NYP-x-SCCCI-
- Branch: "v2DocuSync-AI-(Vance)" (keep the quotes in shell). Origin: github.com/Croptics/VJMDynamics-NYP-x-SCCCI-
- MY files only (never edit teammate files): backend/routes/vance.js; frontend/src/lib/{claudeParse,messagesApi,callManager}.js; frontend/src/pages/{OnboardingPage,BoardingPassesView,ChatAssistantPage}.jsx; frontend/src/components/{TripPulse,ChatBubble}.jsx + frontend/src/components/mchat/* (AssistantConversation, HumanThread, GroupThread, MusterChatInbox, VideoCallOverlay, DocShareCard); frontend/src/pages/mobile/MobileAssistantPage.jsx; INTEGRATION_NOTES_VANCE.md; docs/vance/; tests/vance/.
- OFF-LIMITS (JQ's/teammates'): App.jsx, components/Layout.jsx, components/Sidebar.jsx, lib/api.js, data.js, auth.js, server.js. To mount anything globally I give JQ a one-liner instead of editing Layout.jsx.

## How to run it (IMPORTANT — DB changed)
- Neon (cloud) hit its transfer quota, so we switched to LOCAL Postgres. backend/.env now has DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:[REDACTED]@localhost:5432/mustergo (Neon line commented out), plus Cloudinary + SMTP keys. Local DB is fresh, so it MUST be seeded once:
    cd backend && npm run seed:team && npm run seed:demo   (creates accounts incl. vance/password123!, jq, desmond, jayden, vimal; loads Beijing trip + delegates)
- Two terminals: `cd backend && npm start` (:4000, wait for "PostgreSQL connected"), `cd frontend && npm run dev` (:5173). Open http://localhost:5173 (plain HTTP on v2, no cert warning). Log in as vance / password123!. Ollama (:11434) powers the AI chat; warm it before demoing.
- Gotcha: single active session per account — logging in bumps token_version and invalidates other tokens.

## What's already built
COMMITTED (166f9aa on v2): MusterChat inbox (AI Trip Assistant + person-to-person messaging + doc-share) replacing the old assistant page; assistant "missing" made single-source (count == list == per-coach, in buildSnapshot); coach-scoped assistant queries ("who's missing from Coach 2?" via findCoachInText); onboarding alert()→inline toast + cancel-parse + trip auto-select; boarding-passes auto-refresh + incremental QR; +10 unit tests; docs. All in vance.js + my frontend files.

UNCOMMITTED working-tree changes on v2 (run `git status`/`git diff` to see; commit when I confirm — I direct commits, don't push unprompted, verify local==remote after any push, keep docs/vance + tests/vance + INTEGRATION_NOTES_VANCE.md updated in the SAME commit):
1. Floating ChatBubble (frontend/src/components/ChatBubble.jsx): global, always-visible AI chatbot launcher. Shows a badge + "N new message → open Messages" pill that navigates to /assistant when someone messages me. Needs a 1-line mount in JQ's Layout.jsx: `import ChatBubble from "./ChatBubble.jsx";` then `<ChatBubble />` right after `</main>`.
2. MusterChatInbox.jsx extracted so the /assistant page AND the bubble share one inbox. AssistantConversation "New" button fixed (always resets to blank, no empty-session clutter). Human thread polls every 1.5s for near-real-time.
3. REAL WebRTC teammate calling: backend signaling relay (call_signals table + POST /api/calls/signal + GET /api/calls/poll in vance.js); lib/callManager.js (singleton RTCPeerConnection over Google STUN, offer/answer/ICE via the relay); VideoCallOverlay.jsx rewritten (incoming ring / outgoing / connected with real remote+local video + mic/cam/flip/hangup); HumanThread call buttons start real calls (staff-only). The global incoming-call poll + overlay live inside ChatBubble, so calling only works once ChatBubble is mounted in Layout.jsx.
4. Group chat: backend chat_groups + chat_group_members tables + /api/groups (create/list/:id/thread/:id/messages/:id/members) — group messages reuse dm_messages with convo_key 'g:<id>'. Frontend: messagesApi group helpers, GroupThread.jsx, MusterChatInbox "Groups" section + "New group" modal (name + staff checklist).
5. Individual-chat UI polish (textured background, avatar empty-state, softer bubbles).

## Data model (all in backend/routes/vance.js, lazily created in ensureReady/init)
dm_messages (1:1 + group via convo_key: 1:1 = sorted 'a:<x>|a:<y>' or 'a:<acct>|d:<delegate>'; group = 'g:<id>'); chat_sessions/chat_messages (AI); call_signals (WebRTC); chat_groups/chat_group_members.

## Verified vs not
Verified: vite build passes, 82 backend unit tests pass, all key endpoints return 200 (health, pulse, roster, messages/contacts+updates, groups, calls/poll, chat/sessions, badges); messaging send/thread, WebRTC signal relay (invite relayed vance→jq), and group create/list/thread/send all API-tested working.
NOT verified (environmental): the live 2-peer video CALL handshake needs two real browsers + cameras (only the signaling is confirmed) — test with vance in one window + jq in an incognito window; and browser click-through automation was flaky so I test via build+API+render.

## Known behavior (not bugs)
- Delegates have no login → messaging them is one-directional and they can't be called. Real two-way + calls are staff↔staff (vance/jq/desmond/jayden/vimal).
- Document parsing uses local Ollama (~60s, sometimes messy) unless ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in backend/.env (then it's Claude — faster/better + enables scanned-passport vision).
- If the UI shows a stale React/HMR error (e.g. an old "fmtDuration" export error), hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) — the production build is clean.

## Roadmap / next steps
Immediate: commit the uncommitted work; get JQ to add the ChatBubble mount; test real calling with two windows. Optional polish: ringtone/vibration on incoming call, "missed call" thread entry, group attachments/calls, per-member group unread badges. Bigger features from our team list: (1) delegate status tracked per venue/leg not just boarding; (2) offline mode for China (localStorage updates offline → sync when back online; Great-Firewall + low-signal handling); (3) company physical-badge identification via QR (extends our scanner); (4) funding-dependent upgrades (production face recognition — Vimal owns the face scanner; WebSocket real-time + media storage; on-site offline hardware; China hosting) + a tiered budget plan (MVP → pilot → funded).

Start by reading git status + INTEGRATION_NOTES_VANCE.md, confirm the app runs, then help me commit the uncommitted work (or whatever I ask next).

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

95	  `QRCheckInPage`) scans that code and registers it through **`POST /api/onboarding/checkin`**
96	  (via `qrCheckin()`), which flips the delegate to `status='PRESENT'` (+coach) and

98	  and JQ's head-count agrees. Jayden dropped his original JSON badge format to
99	  standardise on this plain code — so **`qr_code`, `/api/onboarding/checkin` and
100	  `qrCheckin()` are load-bearing for the scanner: do not remove them.**
101	  (There is no separate "scan" tab on the Onboarding screen — the real scanner is
102	  the shared check-in page; Onboarding only *issues* the passes.)
103	- **The chatbot reads a live snapshot assembled from everyone's data:** delegate
104	  roster + coach counts (JQ/Desmond), open exception tickets (Jayden), check-in
105	  method breakdown (`check_in_logs`), and today's itinerary (Desmond). Every
106	  cross-feature read is `try/catch`-isolated, so a missing teammate table never
107	  breaks the chat. Only this developer-authored snapshot reaches the model — it
108	  cannot query arbitrary rows. **The snapshot is scoped to the Beijing study
109	  mission (`t-1`)** — `buildSnapshot()` passes `resolveTripUuid("t-1")` to

113	- **Trip scoping uses `resolveTripUuid()`** (a local helper in `vance.js` — kept
114	  self-contained rather than editing JQ's `data.js`) everywhere a trip id arrives
115	  from the client: `onboarding/confirm`, `onboarding/context`, `onboarding/badges`.
116	  It resolves the trip by **either** the `trips.id` string (`"t-1"`, the base trip)
117	  **or** its `uuid_id` — which is what `GET /all-trips` returns as `id` and what the
118	  Onboarding trip picker now sends. A raw `trips WHERE id = $1` lookup silently
119	  matched nothing for non-base trips and orphaned the delegates (created with a null
120	  `trip_id`), so `confirm` now also **returns `404 UNKNOWN_TRIP`** instead of writing

126	
127	Created lazily on first use by `ensureReady()` in `vance.js`:
128

130	  passport_expiry, role, industry, email, phone, website, qr_code`
131	  (+ a partial unique index on `qr_code`). Reuses Desmond's existing `company`.
132	- `chat_sessions` (incl. `pinned`), `chat_messages` for saved assistant history.

134	## AI providers (deliberate, cost-aware split)
135	
136	- **Document parsing — text-first, vision-fallback (hybrid):**
137	  1. PDFs are read as **text server-side** with `unpdf`. If real text is present
138	     (delegate directories, attendee lists, spreadsheet exports), it's structured by
139	     an LLM as text — cheap, fast, page-by-page, and runs on free local Ollama.
140	  2. Scanned images (no extractable text) fall back to **vision**: Claude vision if

144	     rasterised; upload them as an image.)
145	  Structuring prefers **Claude if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set** (best accuracy), else
146	  Ollama `OLLAMA_PARSE_MODEL` (default `llama3.2`, 3B). Bilingual (中文/English)
147	  names collapse to the romanised name; placeholder/garbage names are dropped.
148	- **Chatbot — Ollama-first, Claude fallback** (mirrors JQ's `insights.js`). Uses
149	  `OLLAMA_MODEL` (`llama3.2:1b` for demo speed); replies **stream token-by-token**
150	  over SSE. Attendance figures are pre-computed into the snapshot ("ready-made
151	  summary" line) so even a small model reports exact numbers — *AI handles language,
152	  code handles arithmetic.*
153	- **Deterministic fast-path (`answerLocally`)** — common factual questions
154	  (attendance, present/missing/unassigned, coach superlatives, company/industry
155	  breakdowns, VIPs, exceptions, itinerary, "who should I worry about", and named
156	  delegate look-ups) are answered **instantly from the snapshot with no model
157	  call** — exact and never hallucinated. Open-ended/generative questions and any
158	  Chinese question return `null` and fall through to the LLM. Applied on
159	  `/chat/messages` and the `/stream` endpoint (which emits the whole answer as one
160	  SSE token); `source:"local"` marks a fast-path reply. Not applied to
161	  `/regenerate` (that always re-attempts via the model). **Because the fast-path
162	  needs no model, the assistant still answers common factual questions even where
163	  no AI engine is reachable** (e.g. the deployed cloud host without Ollama) —
164	  open-ended questions then return a graceful "text engine unavailable here"
165	  message (`source:"unavailable"`) instead of an error.
166	- **Passport-expiry validation (`checkPassportExpiry`)** flags delegates whose
167	  passport is **expired** or **expiring within 6 months** (the standard overseas
168	  rule); missing/unparseable dates are never flagged. Surfaced three ways: a
169	  review-time pill on the onboarding cards (catch it before confirm), a fast-path
170	  assistant intent ("any passport issues?"), and a `computeRisk` item (expired =
171	  critical, expiring = medium) so it appears in the "what to watch" widget too.
172	- **Risk scoring (`computeRisk`)** ranks what to worry about from the live
173	  snapshot — missing VIPs and CRITICAL exceptions first, then the coach furthest
174	  from boarded, then ordinary open tickets. It powers the fast-path "who should I
175	  worry about" answer *and* a ranked `PRIORITIES` block in the model prompt, so
176	  both the instant and the LLM answers lead with the same computed judgement.
177	- **Snapshot cache + model warm-up (speed):** `getSnapshot()` caches the ~6-query
178	  snapshot for 5s (invalidated on confirm and QR check-in, so the bot never shows
179	  stale counts after a write); a fire-and-forget warm-up call on first module use
180	  preloads the chat model so the first question doesn't pay the ~20-30s cold load.
181	
182	## Edge cases handled
183	
184	- **Low-confidence extraction:** rows below the threshold are flagged "Needs review"
185	  and are editable inline; the model returns `null` rather than inventing a field.
186	- **Directory with no passport numbers:** missing passport fields don't force review.
187	- **Big documents:** async job with progress; the admin can leave the page and
188	  re-attach — parsing continues server-side.
189	- **Duplicates:** rows already in the trip are flagged and skipped on confirm; the
190	  Confirm button disables when there's nothing new to add.
191	- **Junk rows:** `onboarding/confirm` skips implausible rows (a name needs ≥2
192	  letters; a ≤2-char single-token name with no company/role/email/phone/passport
193	  is treated as a stray test entry) and returns `skippedInvalid` alongside `added`
194	  so the UI can report how many were dropped. Conservative — real short names
195	  like "Wu"/"Ng" pass whenever the row carries any supporting field.
196	- **Unknown / already-scanned QR:** check-in returns a clear message (404 unknown,
197	  "already boarded" otherwise), and resolves the trip from the delegate's own record
198	  so a mistyped `tripId` can't file a check-in against the wrong trip.
199	- **5-status compatibility (read side):** the team's integration introduced
200	  `ARRIVED`/`ASSIGNED`/`LATE` alongside the legacy `PRESENT`/`MISSING`. My read
201	  paths treat **`PRESENT` and `ARRIVED` both as "boarded"** (badges present-count,
202	  check-in `alreadyBoarded` + counts, boarding-pass status labels + filter, and
203	  the assistant's person/VIP status lines), so a delegate a teammate's scanner
204	  marks `ARRIVED` still reads correctly here. My check-in still *writes* `PRESENT`
205	  (which the team's app accepts as the legacy value). To keep every one of my own
206	  surfaces consistent, `buildSnapshot()` computes its **own** 5-status KPIs from
207	  the scoped roster (boarded = `PRESENT`+`ARRIVED`, unassigned = no coach, missing
208	  = the rest) rather than JQ's `getDashboard` (which counts `PRESENT` only on this
209	  branch) — so the assistant, Trip Pulse widget, and boarding-pass counts all agree.
210	- **AI busy vs not configured:** the assistant distinguishes "busy, try again"
211	  (Ollama up but slow) from "not configured" (nothing installed).
212	- **Ambiguous chatbot query:** the prompt asks ONE clarifying question rather than
213	  guessing; out-of-scope questions are politely declined.
214	
215	## Env (`backend/.env`, see `.env.example`)
216	
217	```
218	DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...neon.tech/...?sslmode=require   # shared team Neon
219	OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:1b        # chatbot model (fast). Omit for llama3.2 (3B, more accurate)
220	# OLLAMA_PARSE_MODEL=llama3.2   # parsing model (defaults to llama3.2 / 3B)
221	# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...  # optional: enables Claude vision (scanned docs) + higher accuracy
222	```
223	
224	The chatbot and text-based parsing work fully offline on Ollama; a Claude key is
225	only needed to read **scanned/image** documents (vision).

  cross-feature read is `try/catch`-isolated, so a missing teammate table never
  breaks the chat. Only this developer-authored snapshot reaches the model — it
  cannot query arbitrary rows. **The snapshot is scoped to the Beijing study
  mission (`t-1`)** — `buildSnapshot()` passes `resolveTripUuid("t-1")` to
  `getTrip/getDashboard/getMissing` and filters the roster by `trip_id`, so the
  assistant + Trip Pulse widgets never mix trips or disagree with the dashboard
  (JQ's `getTrip/getDashboard` default to an arbitrary `LIMIT 1` trip otherwise).
- **Trip scoping uses `resolveTripUuid()`** (a local helper in `vance.js` — kept
  self-contained rather than editing JQ's `data.js`) everywhere a trip id arrives
  from the client: `onboarding/confirm`, `onboarding/context`, `onboarding/badges`.
  It resolves the trip by **either** the `trips.id` string (`"t-1"`, the base trip)
  **or** its `uuid_id` — which is what `GET /all-trips` returns as `id` and what the
  Onboarding trip picker now sends. A raw `trips WHERE id = $1` lookup silently
  matched nothing for non-base trips and orphaned the delegates (created with a null
  `trip_id`), so `confirm` now also **returns `404 UNKNOWN_TRIP`** instead of writing
  orphans when a trip can't be resolved. The Onboarding trip picker fetches the
  **real** trip list (`GET /all-trips`), not the old hardcoded `t-1/t-2/t-3` stub
  (whose `t-2`/`t-3` matched no row in the shared DB).

## Additive schema (never drops/changes base tables)

Created lazily on first use by `ensureReady()` in `vance.js`:

- `delegates`: `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for `passport_no, nationality,
  passport_expiry, role, industry, email, phone, website, qr_code`
  (+ a partial unique index on `qr_code`). Reuses Desmond's existing `company`.
- `chat_sessions` (incl. `pinned`), `chat_messages` for saved assistant history.

## AI providers (deliberate, cost-aware split)

- **Document parsing — text-first, vision-fallback (hybrid):**
  1. PDFs are read as **text server-side** with `unpdf`. If real text is present
     (delegate directories, attendee lists, spreadsheet exports), it's structured by
     an LLM as text — cheap, fast, page-by-page, and runs on free local Ollama.
  2. Scanned images (no extractable text) fall back to **vision**: Claude vision if
     `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, else **local Tesseract OCR** (`method: "ocr/tesseract"`)
     so passport/ID photos and photographed lists work fully offline — the OCR text
     flows through the same structuring step. (Scanned image-only PDFs aren't
     rasterised; upload them as an image.)
  Structuring prefers **Claude if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set** (best accuracy), else
  Ollama `OLLAMA_PARSE_MODEL` (default `llama3.2`, 3B). Bilingual (中文/English)
  names collapse to the romanised name; placeholder/garbage names are dropped.
- **Chatbot — Ollama-first, Claude fallback** (mirrors JQ's `insights.js`). Uses
  `OLLAMA_MODEL` (`llama3.2:1b` for demo speed); replies **stream token-by-token**
  over SSE. Attendance figures are pre-computed into the snapshot ("ready-made
  summary" line) so even a small model reports exact numbers — *AI handles language,
  code handles arithmetic.*
- **Deterministic fast-path (`answerLocally`)** — common factual questions
  (attendance, present/missing/unassigned, coach superlatives, company/industry
  breakdowns, VIPs, exceptions, itinerary, "who should I worry about", and named
  delegate look-ups) are answered **instantly from the snapshot with no model
  call** — exact and never hallucinated. Open-ended/generative questions and any
  Chinese question return `null` and fall through to the LLM. Applied on
  `/chat/messages` and the `/stream` endpoint (which emits the whole answer as one
  SSE token); `source:"local"` marks a fast-path reply. Not applied to
  `/regenerate` (that always re-attempts via the model). **Because the fast-path
  needs no model, the assistant still answers common factual questions even where
  no AI engine is reachable** (e.g. the deployed cloud host without Ollama) —
  open-ended questions then return a graceful "text engine unavailable here"
  message (`source:"unavailable"`) instead of an error.
- **Passport-expiry validation (`checkPassportExpiry`)** flags delegates whose
  passport is **expired** or **expiring within 6 months** (the standard overseas
  rule); missing/unparseable dates are never flagged. Surfaced three ways: a
  review-time pill on the onboarding cards (catch it before confirm), a fast-path
  assistant intent ("any passport issues?"), and a `computeRisk` item (expired =
  critical, expiring = medium) so it appears in the "what to watch" widget too.
- **Risk scoring (`computeRisk`)** ranks what to worry about from the live
  snapshot — missing VIPs and CRITICAL exceptions first, then the coach furthest
  from boarded, then ordinary open tickets. It powers the fast-path "who should I
  worry about" answer *and* a ranked `PRIORITIES` block in the model prompt, so
  both the instant and the LLM answers lead with the same computed judgement.
- **Snapshot cache + model warm-up (speed):** `getSnapshot()` caches the ~6-query
  snapshot for 5s (invalidated on confirm and QR check-in, so the bot never shows
  stale counts after a write); a fire-and-forget warm-up call on first module use
  preloads the chat model so the first question doesn't pay the ~20-30s cold load.

## Edge cases handled

- **Low-confidence extraction:** rows below the threshold are flagged "Needs review"
  and are editable inline; the model returns `null` rather than inventing a field.
- **Directory with no passport numbers:** missing passport fields don't force review.
- **Big documents:** async job with progress; the admin can leave the page and
  re-attach — parsing continues server-side.
- **Duplicates:** rows already in the trip are flagged and skipped on confirm; the
  Confirm button disables when there's nothing new to add.
- **Junk rows:** `onboarding/confirm` skips implausible rows (a name needs ≥2
  letters; a ≤2-char single-token name with no company/role/email/phone/passport
  is treated as a stray test entry) and returns `skippedInvalid` alongside `added`
  so the UI can report how many were dropped. Conservative — real short names
  like "Wu"/"Ng" pass whenever the row carries any supporting field.
- **Unknown / already-scanned QR:** check-in returns a clear message (404 unknown,
  "already boarded" otherwise), and resolves the trip from the delegate's own record
  so a mistyped `tripId` can't file a check-in against the wrong trip.
- **5-status compatibility (read side):** the team's integration introduced
  `ARRIVED`/`ASSIGNED`/`LATE` alongside the legacy `PRESENT`/`MISSING`. My read
  paths treat **`PRESENT` and `ARRIVED` both as "boarded"** (badges present-count,
  check-in `alreadyBoarded` + counts, boarding-pass status labels + filter, and
  the assistant's person/VIP status lines), so a delegate a teammate's scanner
  marks `ARRIVED` still reads correctly here. My check-in still *writes* `PRESENT`
  (which the team's app accepts as the legacy value). To keep every one of my own
  surfaces consistent, `buildSnapshot()` computes its **own** 5-status KPIs from
  the scoped roster (boarded = `PRESENT`+`ARRIVED`, unassigned = no coach, missing
  = the rest) rather than JQ's `getDashboard` (which counts `PRESENT` only on this
  branch) — so the assistant, Trip Pulse widget, and boarding-pass counts all agree.
- **AI busy vs not configured:** the assistant distinguishes "busy, try again"
  (Ollama up but slow) from "not configured" (nothing installed).
- **Ambiguous chatbot query:** the prompt asks ONE clarifying question rather than
  guessing; out-of-scope questions are politely declined.

## Env (`backend/.env`, see `.env.example`)

```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...neon.tech/...?sslmode=require   # shared team Neon
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:1b        # chatbot model (fast). Omit for llama3.2 (3B, more accurate)
# OLLAMA_PARSE_MODEL=llama3.2   # parsing model (defaults to llama3.2 / 3B)
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...  # optional: enables Claude vision (scanned docs) + higher accuracy
```

The chatbot and text-based parsing work fully offline on Ollama; a Claude key is
only needed to read **scanned/image** documents (vision).

# Unit tests — Vance (Document Parsing + Trip Assistant)

Unit tests for my individual code contributions (Screen 4 — Document Parsing /
Onboarding, and the confirm-time data-quality guard). They exercise the **pure,
side-effect-free helpers** in `backend/routes/vance.js` directly, so no database
or HTTP server is needed and every run is deterministic.

## How to run

From the repository root:

```bash
node --test "tests/vance/*.test.js"
```

Uses Node's **built-in test runner** (`node:test` + `node:assert`, Node 18+) —
no external test framework or extra dependencies. `tests/vance/package.json`
sets `"type": "module"` so these files can import the ESM backend modules.

## What's covered

| File | Function under test | What it verifies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `document-parsing.test.js` | `extractRecords` | Pulls a records array out of a raw LLM reply — bare array, ```` ```json ```` fence, `{records:[…]}` wrapper, prose around the array, stray-bracket fallback, and `null` for unparseable/empty input. |
| | `cleanName` | Keeps the romanised half of a bilingual `陈伟 / Reyes Tin` name, leaves pure romanised/pure-CJK names alone, and rejects placeholders (`N/A`, `Not specified`, `unknown`). |
| | `dedupeByName` | Collapses the same person (case-insensitively) keeping the record with more fields; drops nameless rows. |
| | `preferRomanised` | Drops stray Chinese-only duplicate rows when a romanised name exists; keeps a wholly-CJK batch intact. |
| | `finalizeRecords` | The full clean → dedupe → prefer pipeline on a realistic bilingual batch. |
| | `toRow` | Confidence clamping (0–1), the `0.6` default, the `needsReview` flag, id prefixing, and empty→`null` coercion. |
| `confirm-guard.test.js` | `isPlausibleDelegate` | Rejects junk rows (`jq`, single char, symbols, digits, bare short names) while keeping genuine short and CJK names, and any row with a supporting field. |

Total: **38 tests**, all passing.
